nodes.description: In patient fetal tissues and fibroblasts lacking functional KIF7, proteolytic processing of full-length GLI3 into the GLI3-R transcriptional repressor is impaired, elevating the GLI3-FL:GLI3-R ratio and causing widespread upregulation of direct and secondary transcriptional targets of GLI1, GLI2, and GLI3. Because developmental patterning of the neural tube, dorsal telencephalic midline, craniofacial primordia, and limb buds depends on precise gradients of GLI3 repressor versus activator activity, this transcriptional deregulation drives both the lethal CNS/craniofacial malformations and limb polydactyly of HLS2.

nodes.description: KIF7, the human ortholog of Drosophila Costal2, is an immotile kinesin-4 protein and a component of the anterograde intraflagellar transport (IFT) machinery of the primary cilium, where it organizes the cilium-tip compartment and regulates the GLI transcription factors of the Hedgehog pathway. In the absence of Hedgehog ligand KIF7 restrains GLI localization and promotes processing of GLI3 into its transcriptional repressor form (GLI3-R); upon pathway activation KIF7 and GLI accumulate at the cilium tip. Biallelic loss-of-function KIF7 mutations abrogate this ciliary regulation, initiating downstream GLI3 processing failure and Hedgehog target gene deregulation.

nodes.description: Homozygous deletion of the first two base pairs of exon 15 of KIF7 (c.2896_2897del, p.Ala966Profs*81), potentially affecting splicing and resulting in premature truncation within the coiled-coil/cargo domain, first identified in the consanguineous Algerian family (family 1) with four affected HLS2 fetuses. The identical homozygous truncating allele was also identified in a 14-year-old boy with liveborn acrocallosal syndrome (individual ACLS-N1 in PMID:21552264) and in a 4-year-old boy born to consanguineous parents (Case 3 in PMID:27081521) who presented with mild dysgenesis of the corpus callosum, facial dysmorphism, and intellectual disability without overt signs of ciliopathy, demonstrating that this single homozygous allele spans both the perinatally lethal HLS2 and mild living ends of the KIF7 spectrum.
